$comment: Advisories deliberately not failing the high+ audit gate, each scoped to one
GHSA id and each with a hard expiry the gate ENFORCES. An expired entry fails
the build exactly like an unallowlisted advisory would — the time box is real,
not a comment. Adding an entry here is an owner-level policy decision, not an
engineering convenience: everything else, including anything newly introduced,
still fails the gate. See scripts/frontend/audit-gate.mjs.

allow.reason: No patched release exists (1.4.0 is latest, still affected). patch-package backports the exact nested DigestAlgorithm element-count guard from digitalbazaar/forge#1152 at ceba34402e329f0365134f23fe19898756527d65 (#3246); installed-library signature regressions cover it. npm still reports the affected package version. Build-time Expo CLI exposure only. No upstream bump removes it: @expo/cli 57.0.30 (latest) still requires node-forge ^1.3.3 and @expo/code-signing-certificates 0.0.7 (latest) requires ^1.4.0, so it cannot be cut out without dropping Expo. Owner renewed the hard expiry 2026-10-16 -> 2026-10-30 on 2026-10-14; re-check npm then per #3023 and remove this entry and the patch when a fixed upstream release ships.

No recognized patched braces release exists (affected <=3.0.3; latest 3.0.3). The existing patch-package postinstall backports the mandatory parser and compile/expand/stringify recursion-depth guard from upstream PR78; installed regressions cover excessive nesting and ordinary behavior (#3280). This does not resolve all expansion/CPU risks or change advisory status. Reached through Expo/Metro and Jest tooling; the web deployment serves the static export through nginx. Owner renewed the hard expiry 2026-10-19 -> 2026-11-02 on 2026-10-20 (the single renewal pre-approved in #3054 on 2026-10-13), after `npm view braces version` still returned 3.0.3 with no patched release. The vulnerability is NOT fixed; re-check npm then and remove the exception per #3054.
